text:
maria: Heads-up: I'm planning a change to the default model selection behavior for unpinned requests. Today unpinned == stable default; proposal is unpinned -> latest minor of the default family. This affects clients that rely on implicit stability. Looking for quick compatibility/comms checks.

jon: Quick Q — is this considered a breaking change? If a user didn't pin, they opted into updates, but some customers treat implicit stability as a contract.

maria: Good point. I think it's a behavioral change, not an API schema change. But we need a deprecation/notice plan and a fallback pin for safety.

rui: Suggest adding an explicit `Accept-Model` semver header as part of the rollout and a server-side `default-model-pin` toggle so we can flip back instantly. Also add telemetry to detect token-level regressions.

jon: +1 on telemetry. We should run diffed evals on our canonical prompt set and track top-level metrics (latency, token cost, top1 match to baseline). Canary only after those pass.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary cluster available in us-west-2. Tag: canary/model-default-flip. Schedule window open 2026-04-01 03:00 UTC.

sylvia: Docs & SDKs: we'll need a clear migration note and an explicit opt-out example: `Accept-Model: pinned=v1.2.3` and an SDK patch that auto-sets pin when customer enables a 'stable-by-default' flag. I'll own docs.

kevin: For Dedicated/Private customers we must surface this as an opt-in change (they control defaults). Ops: send a targeted email + advisory 30d before. Enterprise CS needs the rollback playbook.

maria: Proposed timeline: announce now in release notes + customer advisory, canary 2 weeks after announcement, 2-week canary at 5% traffic, 90-day full migration window unless rolling back. Rollback circuit: server toggle + purge cache + pin fallback. Thoughts?

jon: Add compatibility tests in CI: run integration suite with `accept-model` unset vs pinned and assert envelope and error shapes unchanged. Also include randomized prompt regression tests.

rui: I'll add a small server-side shim that, for 60s after a model variant returns a different response shape, logs a `compat-shape` alert to notify oncall and sprints. Example shim snippet:

```
# pseudocode
resp = serve(request)
if response_shape(resp) != baseline_shape(request):
  log('compat-shape', request.id, model_version)
  metrics.increment('compat.shape_mismatch')
```

maria: Nice. Who's taking the rollout PRs? I can do the server toggle + docs blurb. Rui will add shape checks and telemetry. Jon — can you own the CI tests & SDK compatibility patch? Sylvia — docs and migration guide? Kevin — CS comms?

jon: I can pick up the CI tests and coordinate SDK patches with devex. Plan: open PRs by EOD Friday.

rui: I'll open telemetry + shim PR tomorrow and wire up a Grafana dashboard alert.

sylvia: Docs PR by next Tues. I'll include a minimal migration snippet and an FAQ section: "Why did the default change? How to pin? How to verify behavior?"

kevin: I'll draft the customer advisory and share it in #customer-success for review. Target send date = announcement + 7 days.

maria: Thanks all. Action items recap in one line: server toggle + rollback PR (maria), CI & SDK tests (jon), shape telemetry + shim (rui), docs & migration guide (sylvia), customer comms (kevin). We'll reconvene async in this thread. :thumbsup:

jon: One more: add a short ML-eval run against 10k prompts with A/B capture to detect quality regressions — low-lift but high value.

maria: Agreed. Add it to the PR checklist.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled canary slot reserved: 2026-04-01 03:00 UTC -> 2026-04-15 03:00 UTC (5% traffic).
